body:
In the streaming branch of `DetokenizerManager._decode_batch_token_id_output`, across consecutive incomplete-UTF-8 (`�`) recovery steps, `sent_offset` is set to `decoded_text_len + len(find_printable_text(new_text))`. `find_printable_text` (`utils.py:377`) is non-monotonic: its penultimate-CJK branch (`:388`) emits through a trailing CJK char, while the later last-space branch (`:392`) retreats to an earlier space, so `len(printable)` can shrink from one recovery step to the next. A shrinking `sent_offset` makes the next clean step's `pending` too small, and it re-emits already-streamed text.

Example `new_text` deltas over three streaming steps: `"A 世�"`, `"A 世a�"`, `"A 世ab"`. Step 1 emits `"A 世"` (`sent_offset=3`); step 2 retreats to `sent_offset=2` (`find_printable_text("A 世a�") == "A "`); step 3 re-emits from offset 2, so the client stream is `"A 世世ab"` instead of `"A 世ab"` — the CJK char is duplicated. This is realistic CJK-plus-byte-BPE streaming traffic. Non-streaming requests are unaffected (they materialize once from the committed text).

Fix (clamp `sent_offset` so it never retreats within a recovery run): #31564.

cc @hnyls2002 @hari-hm
title: Streaming detokenization can duplicate a character (sent_offset retreats across recovery steps)
